description: Unauthorized S3 Bucket Access and Object Manipulation The ECS Task Role has broad permissions to read and write to both S3 buckets. Without proper bucket policy controls or application-level access scoping, a compromised worker could access or modify any object in the buckets. An attacker who compromises a Git Worker container could exploit the broad IAM permissions to access repositories they shouldn't have access to or modify objects in the large object store.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement S3 bucket policy with strict path-based access control
recommendation: Implement request signing and validation for S3 operations

description: Multi-Tenant Data Leakage in S3 Buckets Multiple repositories share the same S3 buckets without proper logical or encryption-based isolation. Path-based separation alone may be insufficient if access controls are misconfigured. A malicious tenant could attempt path traversal or exploit misconfigured bucket policies to access another tenant's repository data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Enhance S3 bucket configuration for multi-tenancy

description: Cache Race Conditions and Data Corruption Multiple Git Workers accessing the Redis cache simultaneously without proper locking mechanisms could lead to race conditions and data inconsistency. An attacker could deliberately trigger concurrent operations to corrupt cache data or cause service disruption.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service

description: DynamoDB Table Data Injection The DynamoDB table could be misused to store sensitive data or executable code, which might be executed by the application logic. An attacker could inject malicious code into metadata fields that might later be executed by application components, or store sensitive credentials that could be extracted.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
recommendation: Implement strict input validation and sanitization
recommendation: Use AWS Secrets Manager for sensitive data

description: Cross-Region Replication Security Cross-region replication of S3 buckets and DynamoDB tables could expose data to different regional security contexts or lead to replication delays affecting consistency. An attacker could exploit differences in regional security controls or target replication delays to access or modify data during transit between regions.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
